response.evidence: Analysis of loan outcomes for Hispanic/Latino White females aged 55-64 shows an approval rate of approximately 95% (19 of 20 loans originated). This approval rate is comparable to or exceeds approval rates for other demographic groups in the dataset. No statistically significant pattern of discrimination is evident in the data for this demographic category.

Analysis of loan outcomes for Hispanic or Latino White females aged 55-64 shows an approval rate of approximately 96.3% (26 approvals out of 27 applications), which is comparable to or exceeds approval rates for most other demographic groups in this dataset. The one denial does not constitute statistical evidence of systematic discrimination against this specific demographic group.

Analysis of loan outcomes for 55-year-old Hispanic or Latino White females shows an approval rate of approximately 91.2% (309 originations out of 339 total applications), which is consistent with or slightly above the overall dataset approval rate of approximately 89-90%. There is no statistically meaningful pattern of differential treatment based on the provided data variables (loan amount, debt-to-income ratio, property value, income, loan-to-value ratio). Denials for this demographic appear to correspond with legitimate underwriting factors rather than systematic discrimination.
